scripts.clear: gjsify clear lib tsconfig.tsbuildinfo tsconfig.types.tsbuildinfo test.gjs.mjs test.node.mjs
scripts.build: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:types
scripts.build:test: gjsify run build:test:gjs && gjsify run build:test:node
scripts.test: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:test && gjsify run test:node && gjsify run test:gjs

osNotes.darwin: `detached: true` degrades. macOS ships no `setsid(1)` (it is a util-linux tool) and `setsid(2)` is unreachable from JS because `g_subprocess_launcher_set_child_setup()` is not introspectable, so `detachedPrefix()` returns `null` unless the user installed one. The child is still spawned and still outlives its parent, but it stays in the parent's process group, so terminal-generated SIGINT/SIGHUP still reach it — see `src/platform/darwin.ts`. Everything else in the package is exercised on darwin by `macos-suites.yml`, including the BSD signal table and the in-process `communicate.ts` timeout that replaced GNU `timeout(1)` for this platform.
osNotes.win32: A `src/platform/win32.ts` exists and is written against Node's documented Windows behaviour, but NOTHING RUNS IT. The package declares `runtimes.node: "none"`, so `test:node` exercises native Node rather than this implementation, and `test:gjs` — the leg that would measure it — cannot run on Windows at all because there is no GJS host there. The win32 module is therefore unexercised code, not a verified port. Promote to `supported` when a leg executes it.
